newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Mosenergo drops annual meeting proposals.
newsitem.headline: Russian Mosenergo drops annual meeting proposals.

text.p: The board of directors of Russian regional power utility Mosenergo on Thursday decided to drop proposals to limit shareholder voting rights and authorise new share issues from the agenda of the annual meeting next week, a company statement said.

"The Board of Directors took the decision to drop from discussion and voting...questions of limiting voting rights of shareholders with stakes larger than one percent... and also the question of authorised shares," the statement said.
A Mosenergo spokesman told Reuters that the company charter would not be materially changed at all.
The board had also recommended an amendment requiring directors to have 25 years of power industry experience.

The statement quoted Mosenergo Chief Executive Nestor Serebryanikov as saying the decision at the board meeting on Thursday was taken as a result of reactions by shareholders and the management of Unified Energy System (UES).
UES holds 49 percent of OAO Energetiki i Elektrifikatsii Mosenergo shares.
"But at the same time, the question of an additional share issue, primarily for parts of the investment programme, is completely relevant," the statement quoted Serebryanikov.
"We intend to bring it up for consideration of shareholders at the next shareholder meeting after additional work," he said.
Foreign shareholders have roundly opposed the proposal which would have required shareholders with more than one percent of stock to get permission from the company to exercise full voting rights.
Many also opposed the proposal to increase authorised capital by 800 million shares, which, if issued, would represent a 30 percent dilution to Mosenergo's 2.56 billion shares.
Mosenergo shares closed on the Russian Trading System before the company announcement at $1.295, up from $1.215 at the close on Wednesday.
